title: Shifted Tate-line endomorphisms on a connected geometric scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $N\ge1$ invertible in $k$, and $B$ a commutative $\mathbf Z/N$-algebra. Let $Y$ be a nonempty connected $k$-scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme]. On its small etale site let $B_Y(1)=\mu_{N,Y}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}B_Y$ and $L=B_Y(r)[d]$ for integers $r\ge0$ and $d$, with tensor-power Tate twist [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and derived shift in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Give $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and $D((\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ the $B$-linear structure induced from their abelian categories of $B$-module sheaves [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. Then the scalar map
$$B\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(L),\qquad b\longmapsto b\,1_L$$
is a bijection. In particular, for any $B$-linear functor [def-weil-linear-category] $G:D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},B)\to D((\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ and any isomorphism $G(L)\cong B_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$, an endomorphism $v:L\to L$ is an isomorphism whenever $G(v)$ is an isomorphism. Here $B$-linear means $G(bf)=bG(f)$ on every morphism group.

proof.text: The constant coefficient module sheaf has scalar endomorphisms. On a connected nonempty scheme the constant module sheaf functor is fully faithful: the unit of its adjunction to evaluation at the terminal etale object is the constant-section map, whose bijectivity is the module-valued version of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected]. Apply [lem-coef-connected-module-constant-sheaf-fully-faithful], attached to the already proved library declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fullyFaithfulModuleConstantSheaf in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.ModulePointFunctions. In ModuleCat B every endomorphism of B is multiplication by its value at 1, including B=0; transport this bijection through the linear constant-sheaf functor.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps, specialized to the additive group of B; agent-written ring-compatibility calculation

proof.text: The structure morphism Y -> Spec k maps the unit N in k to a unit in Gamma(Y,O_Y). Take the named signed multiplication projection p of finiteEtaleTwistPullbackData, the structured API of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For F=B_Y(r), the isomorphisms p(r,-r) and p(-r,r), followed by the exponent-zero identification with B_Y, make B_Y(-r) a two-sided tensor inverse. Tensoring on the left with F is consequently a linear equivalence: its inverse tensors with B_Y(-r), and the unit and counit are the associator, the two multiplication isomorphisms and the unitors. The library TensorInverse.fullyFaithfulTensorLeft implements this elementary construction. Transfer the scalar-endomorphism bijection on B_Y along this functor and then the right unitor F tensor B_Y -> F. No local bases or gluing of endomorphisms are required.

source.place: Tate rank-one reduction; agent-written tensor equivalence argument using the signed multiplication clause of lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], the degree-zero embedding is fully faithful. This functor is B-linear by the induced derived linear structure [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. Transfer the scalar bijection through it and then through the fully faithful linear shift [d] of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Transfer through a fully faithful linear functor works because its map on endomorphisms is a bijection and sends b times the identity to b times the identity. This proves the first assertion. The same argument on the constant sheaf over Spec k, with the derived-unit comparison singleFunctorObjUnitIso, computes the scalar endomorphisms of the constant coefficient complex.

source.place: Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2), degree-zero full faithfulness; agent-written local-basis calculation using the Tate-line statement and the sheaf axiom

proof.text: Transport the scalar bijection of the constant coefficient complex through G(L) isomorphic to B_Spec(k). Linearity gives G(b id_L)=b id_G(L). Since both scalar maps are bijective, G.map from End(L) to End(G(L)) is injective and surjective. Lift the inverse of G(v) to w in End(L); applying G to v composed with w and w composed with v gives the identity. Injectivity gives v composed with w=id and w composed with v=id, so v is an isomorphism. This avoids choosing a scalar inverse as a unit. All constructions include the zero ring and r=0.

proof_origin.place: G3 Lean proof, 2026-10-19: scalar endomorphisms transported through the constant-sheaf functor, tensoring with the Tate line, the degree-zero embedding and shift. The two-sided tensor inverse is obtained from the signed multiplication clause of lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback. Invertibility is reflected by lifting the inverse through the resulting bijection on endomorphisms. This replaces the agent-written local-basis proof plan, and preserves the unit route.

That paragraph does not contain the scalar argument, so the agent-written proof origin is correct. The statement is true: End(B_Y(r)[d]) = End of an invertible B_Y-module = Gamma(Y,B_Y), which is B on a connected Y. I tested B=0, N=1, r=0, d of both signs, Y=Spec k and Y=A^r. Connectedness and nonemptiness are both needed: two points give B x B, and the empty scheme breaks injectivity. In step 1 the local-basis gluing (a_j u_ij = u_ij a_i, so a_j = a_i) is correct. Step 2 is correct: the connected-sections node holds for any abelian group, and the module structure goes through the same constant-section map. Step 3 applies the already-proved first assertion on Spec k, so it is not circular. No duplicate exists: lem-pur-lisse-rank-one-aut covers only finite-stage pro-etale sheaves on separated finite-type schemes. No new nodes and no SGA.
